[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"VPN Configuration (OpenVPN, WireGuard) in Linux"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a comprehensive guide to configuring VPNs using OpenVPN and WireGuard on Linux systems. We will cover installation, configuration, and basic troubleshooting."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"OpenVPN Configuration"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"OpenVPN is a robust and widely used open-source VPN solution. It supports various security protocols and is highly configurable."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Installation"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Install the OpenVPN package using your distribution's package manager. For Debian/Ubuntu systems, use:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"sudo apt update
sudo apt install openvpn easy-rsa"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"For CentOS/RHEL systems, use:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"sudo yum install epel-release
sudo yum install openvpn easy-rsa"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Generating Certificates and Keys (using Easy-RSA)"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Easy-RSA simplifies the process of creating the necessary certificates and keys for OpenVPN. First, copy the Easy-RSA scripts to a secure location:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"make-cadir ~/openvpn-ca"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"cd ~/openvpn-ca"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Initialize the PKI:"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"./easyrsa init-pki"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Build the Certificate Authority (CA):"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"./easyrsa build-ca"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generate the server certificate and key:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"./easyrsa build-server-full server nopass"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generate the client certificate and key:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"./easyrsa build-client-full client1 nopass"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generate Diffie-Hellman parameters:"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"./easyrsa gen-dh"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generate a TLS authentication key:"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"openvpn --genkey --secret ta.key"},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"OpenVPN Server Configuration"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create the server configuration file (e.g., /etc/openvpn/server.conf) and add the following configuration. Adjust the network settings as needed:"},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"port 1194
proto udp
dev tun
ca /root/openvpn-ca/pki/ca.crt
cert /root/openvpn-ca/pki/issued/server.crt
key /root/openvpn-ca/pki/private/server.key  # This file should be kept secret
dh /root/openvpn-ca/pki/dh.pem
server 10.8.0.0 255.255.255.0
ifconfig-pool-persist ipp.txt
push "redirect-gateway def1 bypass-dhcp"
push "dhcp-option DNS 8.8.8.8"
push "dhcp-option DNS 8.8.4.4"
keepalive 10 120
tls-auth ta.key 0 # This file is secret
cipher AES-256-CBC
auth SHA256
user nobody
group nogroup
persist-key
persist-tun
status openvpn-status.log
log-append  openvpn.log
verb 3
explicit-exit-notify 1"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"Enable IP forwarding:"},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"To make it permanent, edit /etc/sysctl.conf and uncomment or add the line: net.ipv4.ip_forward=1"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"Configure the firewall to allow OpenVPN traffic. For example, using iptables:"},{"order":33,"type":"code","text":"sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.8.0.0/24 -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.8.0.0/24 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -d 10.8.0.0/24 -j ACCEPT"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'eth0' with your internet-facing interface. Save the iptables rules to make them persistent across reboots."},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start the OpenVPN server:"},{"order":36,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl start openvpn@server"},{"order":37,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl enable openvpn@server"},{"order":38,"type":"subheading","text":"OpenVPN Client Configuration"},{"order":39,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a client configuration file (e.g., client1.ovpn) with the following content. Replace 'your_server_ip' with the actual IP address or hostname of your OpenVPN server:"},{"order":40,"type":"code","text":"client
dev tun
proto udp
remote your_server_ip 1194
resolv-retry infinite
nobind
persist-key
persist-tun
ca ca.crt
cert client1.crt
key client1.key
tls-auth ta.key 1
cipher AES-256-CBC
auth SHA256
remote-cert-tls server
verb 3"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"Copy the client certificate (client1.crt), key (client1.key), CA certificate (ca.crt), and ta.key to the client machine. Ensure the paths in the client configuration file match the location of these files."},{"order":42,"type":"paragraph","text":"Connect to the VPN using the OpenVPN client:"},{"order":43,"type":"code","text":"sudo openvpn --config client1.ovpn"},{"order":44,"type":"subheading","text":"WireGuard Configuration"},{"order":45,"type":"paragraph","text":"WireGuard is a modern VPN protocol known for its simplicity and high performance."},{"order":46,"type":"subheading","text":"Installation"},{"order":47,"type":"paragraph","text":"Install the WireGuard package using your distribution's package manager. For Debian/Ubuntu systems, use:"},{"order":48,"type":"code","text":"sudo apt update
sudo apt install wireguard"},{"order":49,"type":"paragraph","text":"For CentOS/RHEL systems, use:"},{"order":50,"type":"code","text":"sudo yum install epel-release
sudo yum install wireguard-tools"},{"order":51,"type":"subheading","text":"Generating Keys"},{"order":52,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generate private and public keys for both the server and the client:"},{"order":53,"type":"code","text":"wg genkey | tee privatekey | wg pubkey > publickey"},{"order":54,"type":"paragraph","text":"Repeat this command on both the server and the client."},{"order":55,"type":"subheading","text":"WireGuard Server Configuration"},{"order":56,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create the server configuration file (e.g., /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf) and add the following configuration. Replace 'your_server_private_key' with the server's private key and 'your_client_public_key' with the client's public key:"},{"order":57,"type":"code","text":"[Interface]
PrivateKey = your_server_private_key
Address = 10.6.0.1/24
ListenPort = 51820
PostUp = iptables -A FORWARD -i wg0 -j ACCEPT; iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE; ip6tables -A FORWARD -i wg0 -j ACCEPT; ip6tables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
PostDown = iptables -D FORWARD -i wg0 -j ACCEPT; iptables -t nat -D POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE; ip6tables -D FORWARD -i wg0 -j ACCEPT; ip6tables -t nat -D POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE

[Peer]
PublicKey = your_client_public_key
AllowedIPs = 10.6.0.2/32"},{"order":58,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'eth0' with your internet-facing interface."},{"order":59,"type":"paragraph","text":"Enable IP forwarding:"},{"order":60,"type":"code","text":"sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1"},{"order":61,"type":"paragraph","text":"To make it permanent, edit /etc/sysctl.conf and uncomment or add the lines: net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 and net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1"},{"order":62,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start the WireGuard interface:"},{"order":63,"type":"code","text":"sudo wg-quick up wg0"},{"order":64,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl enable wg-quick@wg0"},{"order":65,"type":"subheading","text":"WireGuard Client Configuration"},{"order":66,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create the client configuration file (e.g., /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf) and add the following configuration. Replace 'your_client_private_key' with the client's private key, 'your_server_public_key' with the server's public key, and 'your_server_ip' with the server's IP address:"},{"order":67,"type":"code","text":"[Interface]
PrivateKey = your_client_private_key
Address = 10.6.0.2/32
DNS = 8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4

[Peer]
PublicKey = your_server_public_key
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0
Endpoint = your_server_ip:51820
PersistentKeepalive = 25"},{"order":68,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start the WireGuard interface:"},{"order":69,"type":"code","text":"sudo wg-quick up wg0"},{"order":70,"type":"subheading","text":"Troubleshooting"},{"order":71,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check firewall rules to ensure VPN traffic is allowed."},{"order":72,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verify that IP forwarding is enabled."},{"order":73,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Examine the VPN server and client logs for errors."},{"order":74,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure that the client configuration file contains the correct server IP address and keys."}]
